hook.headline: Intercept the dangerous action before it runs
altHeadlines: The approval layer for unattended agents
Away from the keyboard is not away from control

audience.who: Developers who run coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw) unattended for hours and cannot watch every call
painPoints: The agent reaches for a deploy, a table drop, a force push or a .env read while nobody is at the keyboard
Local permission prompts only work for the operator sitting at the terminal
Interrupt too often and the policies get switched off; the maintainer turned every policy off for 18 days after false interruptions
A log of what already ran is not control over what runs next

objections.objection: My CLI already prompts me before dangerous commands
objections.response: Those prompts serve the person at the keyboard. DashClaw holds the action and lets you approve minutes or hours later, from wherever you are
Approve and deny decisions feed a calibration loop; an interruption has to earn its cost, and nothing is blocked outright by default

objections.objection: Is this just another audit log
objections.response: DashClaw holds the real command before it runs and binds the release to a recorded human decision. The ledger is what was stopped and released, not a log after the fact

switchingForces.push: An unattended agent did something irreversible, or the fear that it will
switchingForces.pull: The dangerous call freezes until a person says yes, and the record proves it
switchingForces.habit: Watching the terminal, or accepting every prompt to make it stop
switchingForces.anxiety: Another layer that blocks work or floods the inbox; answered by hold-not-block and the calibration loop

features.heading: Intercept and hold
benefitLines: Sensitive actions are held before they run
Risk scored and bound to the exact command
One click to allow or deny in the inbox
features.rationale: The hero surface. The README's core promise (hold it before it runs, ask you first) is literally this inbox; the demo footage shows a held deploy action resolved with one click.

features.heading: Recorded and verified
benefitLines: Every governed action lands in one ledger
Chained to the decision that allowed it
Verified where receipts are issued, spend and risk on the record
features.rationale: The trust half of the loop: approval alone is a gate, the causal chain is the proof. Differentiates from log viewers because entries bind to the decision that released them. Verification is conditional in the thesis (receipts where issued), so the line says so.

positioning.differentiator: DashClaw governs the action itself. It holds the real command before it runs and binds the release to a recorded human decision, instead of showing you a log of what already happened.

narration.text: At three in the morning, your agent is still working.
It reads. It writes. It deploys. Nobody is watching.
Until it reaches for something that cannot be undone.
DashClaw holds it. Risk scored, bound to the exact command. Waiting for you, wherever you are.
One click. It runs. And the decision is on the record.
Every governed action, chained to the decision that allowed it. Not a log after the fact.
Govern your agents at dashclaw dot io.
